topics.label: Introduction to the Lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the students and frames the challenge and importance of studying the complement system.

topics.label: Principles and Organization of the Complement System
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental architecture, nomenclature rules, and central C3 activation mechanism underlying the complement cascade.

topics.label: Complement Activation Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three pathways that initiate complement recognition and converge on the generation of C3 convertases at a trigger threshold.

topics.label: Effector Mechanisms of Activated Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the primary downstream processes through which activated complement destroys pathogens and enhances the immune response.

topics.label: Host Protection and Complement Regulation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and inhibitory mechanisms that prevent complement from damaging host cells.

topics.label: Clinical Manifestations of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how genetic or acquired deficiencies in distinct complement components lead to specific infection susceptibilities and immune complex diseases.

topics.label: Pathogen Strategies for Complement Evasion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the evolutionary adaptations pathogens use to circumvent complement-mediated clearance, highlighting Staphylococcus aureus as a primary example.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides standard closing remarks, concluding the lecture and previewing the next topic in the course series.
